subject: Decisioning: Dedicated capacity vs Private deployment — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@aurorafin.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Decisioning: Dedicated capacity vs Private deployment — recap & next steps

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a suggested set of next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Workloads: low-latency real-time scoring for fraud detection (99th pctl target ~75ms), plus nightly batch embedding jobs (large batch sizes).
- Data constraints: EU data residency, customer PII stored behind customer keys (KMS).
- Traffic profile: steady 200 RPS sustained with 6x peaks around marketing campaigns.

Deployment options we recommend exploring
1) Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) — reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, fast time-to-market, managed by Redwood. Shorter onboarding (2–4 weeks) but requires a contract commitment.
2) Private (VPC / private control plane) — runs in your VPC (or air-gapped on-prem if required), full customer control over networking and keys, best fit for strict compliance but longer procurement/onboarding (6–12+ weeks).

Open questions for prioritization
- Which is higher priority: latency SLA/cost predictability (leans Dedicated) or full network/data isolation and KMS control (leans Private)?
- Procurement timeline constraint (when do you expect to have a PO/signature)? You mentioned targeting end of Q4 — can you confirm?

Proposed next steps
- If prioritizing time-to-value, propose a short pilot on Dedicated (2–4 weeks).
- If compliance is gating, we can begin Private scoping and SOW prep — I can loop in Rohan (SRE) for network design.
- Marcus attached a brief pricing range and our SOC2 report; I’ve also attached a one-pager comparing both options and a draft mutual action plan (MAP).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-one-pager.pdf, initial-map.xlsx
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD_AURORA

Can you confirm which path you want us to prioritize and the procurement target date? Happy to set up a 30-min follow-up next week.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@aurorafin.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T11:30:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Decisioning: Dedicated capacity vs Private deployment — recap & next steps

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Procurement: we are still aiming for a decision by the end of Q4, but procurement will only start once we have a clear pricing and a short MAP to present to finance.
- Security: we need the SOC2 report (redacted okay) and a short note on how KMS is integrated for Private — specifically, does Private require on-prem hardware or can it be customer-hosted in our VPC?
- Technical: can you share expected P95/P99 latency numbers for the Dedicated option at the scale described?

Samir (CC'd) will lead procurement — Samir, looping you in. Let us know what you need to move this forward.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Data Platforms, Aurora Financial
elena.rossi@aurorafin.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@aurorafin.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decisioning: Dedicated capacity vs Private deployment — recap & next steps

Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the questions — quick answers inline and attaching the requested artifacts.

- SOC2: attached a redacted SOC2 report (SOC2-redacted.pdf).
- Private deployment: Private is available as a customer-hosted VPC deployment (no mandatory on-prem hardware). We support both customer VPC-hosted Private and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. Keys: you can bring your own KMS (customer-managed keys) and we support HSM integrations for Private.
- Dedicated performance: at the scale described (sustained 200 RPS with 6x peaks) we typically observe P95 latencies in the 35–70ms range and P99 under 120ms for optimized models on Dedicated with continuous batching. Exact numbers vary by model, sequence length and batching policy — we can run a short profiling pilot to produce a deterministic SLA for your workload.

Attached: pricing-range.xlsx, SOC2-redacted.pdf
DocuSign (placeholder for SOW): https://www.docusign.com/xyz/placeholder

If helpful, I can share a short TCO sketch vs self-hosting. Otherwise, the two next practical steps are: 1) NDA/PO to get to detailed pricing and contractual terms; 2) schedule a network/SRE call with Rohan to begin Private scoping if you want to pursue that path.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Quick check-in: procurement timing & next steps (bump)

Hi Elena —

Wanted to check in briefly — I haven’t heard back since Marcus shared the pricing and SOC2 (thanks Marcus). A few notes and a proposed short set of options so we can keep this moving toward your end-of-Q4 target: 

- If procurement is the gating item, would you like a one-page MAP and an estimated SOW to take to finance this week? We can have a draft over to you in 48 hours.
- If compliance scoping is the gating item, we can schedule a 30-min network call with Rohan next week to walk through VPC/KMS questions and list out any required artifacts.
- Open to a short profiling pilot on Dedicated to generate deterministic latency numbers (2–4 week pilot).

Does the end-of-Q4 timeline still look realistic on your side? If so, what is the immediate next step you prefer (MAP, SOW, SRE call, NDA)?

If I don’t hear back, I’ll assume you’d like us to prepare a one-page MAP and a tentative SOW for finance and will send that by EOD Wednesday — happy to adjust based on what you need.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Calendly: https://calendly.com/jasmine-redwood/30min
